glyphs.notes: Use a five-column shared body derived from the paired native a/turned-a cap and stave entrances, with two equal six-pixel counters and a compact two-row waist. The left shoulder enters below its crest; the right hip leaves above the baseline. Joined staves retain simple native n/m/u endings. Middle components follow allocation order from left to right; only their designated upper or lower extension pixels change between states. Outer curved terminals use the approved dense-family hook and simple eng return; no extra tip, serif, or enclosed terminal pocket is added. This allocation contains no declared long bowl or returnContact, so ordinary compact hooks are not forced to close against unrelated staves.

Middle components follow allocation order from left to right; only their designated upper or lower extension pixels change between states. Outer curved terminals use the native-f crest and contextual native-y or script-g return; no extra serif is added. This allocation contains no declared long bowl or returnContact, so ordinary compact hooks are not forced to close against unrelated staves. The listed outer-stave joining pixels continue straight extensions through a rounded native cap or return. The lower bowl closes at row 12 and carries the complete script-g tail; the short left leg leaves row 13 open. Its independent descender includes a documented row-13 bridge, whose contact with the upturn naturally adds a terminal pocket.

glyphs.notes: Four staves occupy columns 1, 3, 5 and 7; column 0 remains blank. The native Unifont m shoulder sequence is compacted to one crest pixel per two-column interval. The initial stave retains its head pixel at (1,6), while internal staves start at row 7 beneath supported diagonal crests. As in native m, joined staves have no additional base serifs. All three underside openings remain open through the baseline; optional middle descenders add only their two designated pixels below it. State: neither middle component extended.
reviewNotes: Each compressed arch retains a one-column aperture from row 7 through row 13.
The top row has two touching pixels only at the initial stave head and first shoulder; the other shoulders use supported diagonal joins.
Independent descenders preserve the complete body and remain separated by a blank column.

glyphs.notes: The turned arches are drawn on the unchanged Latin body rows, following native turned m and u hips, rather than rotating the entire 16-row cell. The long left bowl occupies columns 1 through 3 from row 3 to row 13. Its one-pixel open return is at (3,5), immediately above the adjacent first middle arm. Extending that arm fills the opening; extending the farther arm at column 5 leaves it open. Compound ascenders use the unadorned vertical terminals of native h and q, avoiding head-serifs that would bridge neighboring staves. State: neither middle component extended.
reviewNotes: The left-only and both states close exactly the same long bowl; the right-only state leaves the opening at (3,5) unchanged.
The first extension overlaps the pre-existing returning terminal at (3,4), so its visible difference adds two pixels, (3,3) and (3,5).
The extended right outer stem reaches rows 3 and 15 without gaining a broad dotless-i foot.

The left spine is drawn explicitly within columns 1–3, retaining the native a lower counter and open upper sweep without extra bulbs or repeated standalone serifs.

groups.title: spine with two stems and tail — independent middle extensions
groups.notes: Four staves use columns 1, 3, 5, 7. Native turned-m/u hips retain body rows 6–13; only the final right stave keeps its baseline pixel. The left spine is drawn explicitly within columns 1–3, retaining the native a lower counter and open upper sweep without extra bulbs or repeated standalone serifs.  The final arm in columns 5–7 follows Unifont y: row 11 retains the two sides, row 12 joins into the right return while retaining the shared stave pixel required by the preceding hip or bowl, rows 13–14 retain the right stave, and row 15 has only the interior return pixels. Only this lower arm and tail adapt to the compact bay; middle extensions remain independent.
